title: Write reusable, typed SQL helpers with SQLite
description: Infer JSON object types from SQLite columns and compose expressions with runtime decoding.

steps.label: Start with SQL
steps.title: Build an object and decode the JSON text
steps.body:
You want a profile with an ID, display name, nullable bio and active flag. This guide uses SQLite and Drizzle ORM **1.0.0-rc.5**. `json_object` builds the object as JSON text, and `.mapWith()` parses that text when Drizzle reads the selected expression.

SQLite stores boolean-mode columns as integers. The `json(case ...)` expression turns those stored values into JSON booleans. The column's normal boolean decoder does not run inside `json_object`.

Press **Run**. Ada has a bio and `active: true`; Grace has `bio: null` and `active: false`. `sql<string>` describes the JSON text before decoding; the parser's return type describes the decoded `Profile`. Parsing JSON does not validate its fields against that type.

meta.summary: Build JSON in SQLite, preserve booleans and decode the selected text.
meta.changed: Two decoded profiles returned with booleans and Grace's null bio.

steps.label: Infer the result
steps.title: Move inference and decoding into one helper
steps.body:
Replace the inline expression with `jsonObject({ ... })`, a custom helper in `helpers.ts`. It infers each result key, column type and nullable field from the argument. There is no separate `Profile` type at the call site.

The helper also handles the SQLite-specific work: constructing JSON, converting boolean-mode columns and parsing the selected JSON text. Hover over `profiles` to see `displayName: string`, `bio: string | null` and `active: boolean`.

Press **Run**. The output stays the same. Rename `displayName` in the argument and the inferred result key follows your selection.

meta.summary: Infer the object type and reuse its JSON decoder without a handwritten result type.
meta.changed: The helper returned the same decoded profiles, including nullable text and booleans.

steps.label: Compose helpers
steps.title: Nest an expression and reuse it in another query
steps.body:
`author` is an ordinary `SQL<T>` expression. The same helper nests it inside each post card and selects it on its own as a profile. A computed `length()` expression supplies `titleLength: number`.

The nested helper call stays a direct `json_object` expression in the generated SQL. SQLite recognizes it as JSON, so the author becomes an object rather than an escaped JSON string. The outer expression's decoder parses the whole result; nested `.mapWith()` decoders do not run independently.

Press **Run**. You get three post cards and two profiles, with the same values as the PostgreSQL version. The inner join guarantees an author. This helper excludes columns from the nullable side of an outer join because the column's declared nullability does not describe that join.

meta.summary: Compose nested JSON and a computed field, then reuse the author expression.
meta.changed: Three cards contain author objects; the same expression also returns two profiles.

steps.label: Read the helper
steps.title: Keep the SQLite representation explicit
steps.body:
Open `helpers.ts`. `Shape` captures the argument's fields. `GetColumnData` keeps each column's type and nullability; `SQL<infer Value>` extracts a computed or nested expression's result type. JSON keys are bound parameters, and columns remain Drizzle SQL fragments.

The helper accepts built-in text, integer and boolean-mode columns. It explicitly converts boolean columns before JSON construction. Dates, blobs, JSON stored in text and custom column decoders need their own representation decisions. A typed SQL expression must also match its actual JSON output.

SQLite treats ordinary text passed to `json_object` as a string, even when that text contains JSON. If you later read an object from a column or subquery and nest it again, wrap that value with SQLite's `json()` function. The direct nested helper calls in this guide already retain their JSON identity.

Fork the guide to keep the composed query and helper. [Open the PostgreSQL version](/examples/reusable-helpers) to compare the same lesson with `jsonb_build_object` and driver-decoded JSON.

meta.summary: Read the inferred type, boolean conversion and JSON text decoder.
